ledger.hypothesis: compute() is not algorithmic here (bench drives reset=1: 20k RNG draws = 43 us); it is Maya per-element API cost -- the builder fill (~190 us) plus the mandatory data.setClean(aSort) over 20k connected elements (0.4-1.2 ms) -- so cutting API calls per element is the only controllable lever. Probe: fill loop 174-250 us -> 126-150 us, and setClean ran cheaper after asFloat writes. ledger.hypothesis: The profile put data.setClean(aSort) at 500-1300 us and I read it as Maya tearing down the replaced 20k-element array, so writing in place would drop both the builder allocations and that teardown. Wrong half: a no-write diagnostic shows setClean is ~260-330 us whether we write or not, so it is Maya's per-plug bookkeeping for 20k connected elements. The measured win is all on our side of the call: builder fill 145 us -> 105 us in place, RNG 42 us -> 24 us, fusing the draw into the write saves another 12-20 us.
ledger.note: confirmed twice (incumbent under the noise floor): 0.533 / 0.672 ms
ledger.risk: The RNG must stay identical per STL. Mt64 is the standard-fixed mt19937_64 (0 mismatches over 40.66M draws against the library engine, 10000th output 9981545732273789042), and it still goes through the library's own uniform_real_distribution, so MSVC's P0952 generate_canonical and libc++'s version each keep their own mapping. In-place writes only happen when every logical 0..n-1 element exists and elementCount == n; any other layout falls back to the original builder path.
ledger.theme: Write the 20k sort[] floats in place through the existing element handles (jumpToElement(i) proves the 0..n-1 layout, builder kept as fallback) instead of rebuilding the whole array with MArrayDataBuilder, and fuse a bit-identical inlined mt19937_64 draw into that write loop.

ledger.hypothesis: The bench holds reset=1 (seeded draw: Random(20260808) -> reset 1), so every tick is a reseed, 20000 draws and 20000 element writes. The first idea was to walk the output array by position with next() instead of 20000 logical jumpToElement(i) searches. It was measured 65% SLOWER (1.02 vs 0.61 ms): on an output MArrayDataHandle, next() and elementIndex() cost more than the jump. Phase timers inside compute() then showed where the time goes: setClean(aSort) about 400 us, write loop about 120 us, RNG about 22 us, everything else under 10 us. setClean costs the same when called before the writes, after them, or with no writes at all, so it is a per-networked-plug DG cost inside Maya.

ledger.risk: None shipped. Rejected on correctness, not speed: writing by physical position (jumpToArrayElement) was 26 us faster, but it needs position p to hold logical index p, and Maya does not document that elements are stored in logical-index order. Checking each element with elementIndex() gives back the whole gain.
